name: Feni district flood

hazard.label: Flood - open water seen by radar

observation.source: ESA Copernicus Sentinel-1, RTC product read from the Microsoft Planetary Computer STAC catalogue (open catalogue, anonymous signing, no account required)
observation.threshold_method: Otsu gave 1.05, outside the plausible 1.1-2.0 range, so the UN-SPIDER default of 1.25 was used instead
observation.method: Speckle filtered with a 50 m median, ratio of the two dates in dB, threshold by Otsu's method, permanent water (JRC Global Surface Water v1.4, over 50% occurrence) and slopes of 5 degrees or more excluded, patches under 8 pixels dropped. Follows the UN-SPIDER recommended practice for SAR flood mapping.
observation.limitations: Detects open water only. Flooded vegetation, flooded cropland and flooded buildings can return MORE radar energy than dry ground (double bounce), so this method misses them rather than flagging them. The flooded area is therefore a lower bound, and it under-counts exactly where people live.
observation.not_ground_truth: A satellite observation, not ground truth. No validated flood map exists for this event, so no accuracy figure is claimed.

context.roads_note: A road is flagged when it crosses an area where the radar saw open water on the observation date. That is not a statement that the road is impassable, and an unflagged road is not confirmed open: radar cannot see water under trees or between buildings, and it knows nothing about depth or current.

terrain.source: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (ESA / Airbus), open data on AWS
terrain.method: Window read of the public tiles, merged to UTM, hillshade at azimuth 315 and altitude 45 degrees, 30 m grid
terrain.limitations: A surface model: it includes buildings and trees and it smooths low flat land. It shows the shape of the ground. It is not a flood model.

optical.source: ESA Copernicus via Microsoft Planetary Computer (open catalogue, no account)
optical.note: Dry-season picture of the landscape, taken before the flood. It is not a picture of the flood.

radar.sensor: Sentinel-1A C-band SAR, VH, RTC gamma-0
radar.note: Radar sees smooth water as dark. These are the same passes the flood layer was computed from, scaled for display only.

usage: Prepared while online, then carried into the field. Once this file is on the device the instrument needs no network: no tiles, no services, no accounts.
